newsitem.title: USA: PSE&G can meet 5-10 pct savings goal.
newsitem.headline: PSE&G can meet 5-10 pct savings goal.

text.p: Public Service Enterprise Group Inc's Public Service Electric and Gas Co said Thurday the goal of five to 10 percent rate reductions for all customers set in the New Jersey Energy Master Plan policy statement can be met.

PSE&G President Lawrence R. Codey said, "While difficult to achieve, we believe a multi-year plan can be structured to achieve significant savings in this range, and we are committed to working toward that target..."
The plan was unveiled Thursday by the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities.
Designed as a blueprint to restructure the electric utility industry in the state, it calls for electric industry deregulation in New Jersey starting in late 1998.

"This is the first step along the way to profound changes in electric service as New Jersey residents know it," said Codey, "and the first time that consumers are going to be allowed to act like consumers in shopping for electricity the same way they now shop for telephone and health care services."

Release of the Master Plan now requires that the state's electric utilities each submit to the BPU a detailed response outlining the actions they will take to deregulate and offer choice to their customers. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
